canonicalExplanation.summary: **Media queries** apply styles when the viewport or user environment matches a condition: width (`(min-width: 48rem)`), colour scheme (`prefers-color-scheme: dark`), contrast (`prefers-contrast: more`), hover capability and more. Choose breakpoints where **your content breaks** — not at guessed device models — and write them in `rem` so they respect text-size settings. Feature queries (`@supports`) apply styles only when the browser understands them.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A team adds breakpoints at 375px ("iPhone"), 768px ("iPad") and 1024px ("laptop"). Then a new phone is 412px wide, and the navigation wraps into three ugly lines between breakpoints. Devices change every year; content doesn't care. Navigation changes layout when its content no longer fits, not at a guessed tablet model width. In this lesson you'll implement and test layout, colour-scheme and contrast adaptations.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **Flexbox and Grid** and **Typography, color and visual treatment** modules, plus **Intrinsic responsive grids** and **Color and contrast**.

sections.heading: The rule: query the environment where the content needs it
Test the environment

includes: Write mobile-first width queries at content breakpoints in rem.
Adapt to prefers-color-scheme and prefers-contrast, and use @supports.

outcomes: Implement and test layout, color-scheme and contrast adaptations.

examples.title: Navigation that changes when it stops fitting
examples.situation: Navigation changes layout when its content no longer fits, not at a guessed tablet model width.
walkthrough: **Find the break:** resizing shows the six links stop fitting on one row below about 46rem.
**Query:** mobile-first column layout, and `@media (min-width: 46rem)` switches to a row.
**Test:** at 412px, 700px and 1000px — and with text at 150% — the browser will render the nav cleanly because the breakpoint follows the content.
examples.result: The navigation switches exactly when its content stops fitting, on any device.

examples.title: Dark mode with unreadable borders
examples.situation: A site adds `prefers-color-scheme: dark` colours, but form input borders stay #d1d5db — nearly invisible on #111827.
walkthrough: Only text and background tokens were overridden.
Input borders fail the 3:1 component contrast on dark backgrounds.
Fix: include --color-border in the dark query, measure it (≥ 3:1), and add a prefers-contrast: more override.
examples.result: Inputs are clearly outlined in light, dark and high-contrast settings.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Media queries should target named devices such as iPhone and desktop.
misconceptions.correction: Devices vary endlessly; layouts should change where their content stops working. Choose content-based breakpoints (in rem), and also respond to user preferences like colour scheme and contrast.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "Navigation that changes when it stops fitting", how was the breakpoint chosen?

analogy.example: Media queries are like **dressing for the weather, not the calendar**: you put on a coat when it's cold (content stops fitting), not on a fixed date (a device width).
usefulFor: preferences are part of the weather
limitations: Weather changes without warning; so do new devices.
@supports is like checking whether the shop sells umbrellas before relying on one.

nearTransfer.prompt: Write queries so a hover-only tooltip style applies only on devices that can hover, and a dark palette applies when the user prefers dark.

farTransfer.prompt: Take a page with device-named breakpoints. Replace them with content-based rem breakpoints, add dark and more-contrast support via tokens, and test all combinations in DevTools.
expectedEvidence: Light, dark and high-contrast all readable.

remediation.explanation: Delete your breakpoints, make the base layout work at 320px, then widen slowly. Add a query only at the width where something looks broken — and write it in rem.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "Dark mode with unreadable borders" too: which tokens are missing?

recap.summary: To implement and test layout, colour-scheme and contrast adaptations, write mobile-first base styles, add rem-based width queries where content breaks, respond to prefers-color-scheme and prefers-contrast through tokens, guard new features with @supports, and test with DevTools emulation.
